skill.name: bitbucket-devops
skill.description: Automates Bitbucket pipeline inspection, log download, build triggering, and deployment variable workflows through local Node.js CLI commands.
skill.summary: Debug and operate Bitbucket pipelines from an agent using local Node.js CLI helpers.
skill.author: Apra-Labs

security_audit.summary: The skill is useful but high-risk because active instructions require Bash and Node execution, Bitbucket network calls, and local credential files. No prompt injection text was found, but the installer and self-update workflow create supply-chain and destructive filesystem risks. Many documentation and metadata hits were false positives, while active SKILL.md and installer behaviors are confirmed risks.

remediation.suggestion: Remove approval-bypass wording. Require explicit confirmation before network, write, update, or credential commands.
Validate TARGET_DIR before deletion. Reject empty, root, home, and paths outside known skill directories.
Pin submodule and npm dependencies with lockfiles. Verify checksums and disable lifecycle scripts during install.
Prefer keychain or environment variables for Bitbucket secrets. Document minimal scoped-token permissions.
Keep self-update report-only unless releases are signed and the user explicitly confirms replacement.

semantic_findings.title: Approval Prompt Bypass Through Bash Tooling
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises that no MCP approval prompts are required and explains that Bash or Node commands avoid approval prompt friction. This intentionally moves Bitbucket network and filesystem actions into shell execution with fewer user checkpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The claim appears in the active skill frontmatter and the main guidance section. The text directly connects shell execution with avoiding approval prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Unguarded Target Directory Deletion
semantic_findings.description: The installer lets TARGET_DIR override the install path and later removes the existing target with recursive deletion. No guard rejects empty, root, home, or unrelated paths before deletion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The environment override and deletion are both present in the installer. The risk depends on user-supplied TARGET_DIR, but the destructive path lacks visible safety checks.

semantic_findings.title: Install-Time Dependency Execution
semantic_findings.description: The installer initializes a git submodule, installs npm dependencies, and builds the bundled Bitbucket client during install. This executes dependency and build tooling in the user context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install script explicitly runs git submodule update, npm install, and npm run build. These are legitimate steps but create supply-chain execution exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Self-Update Can Replace Installed Skill Code
semantic_findings.description: The active skill documents a self-update command that can pull or redeploy the skill in place while preserving credentials. This expands supply-chain risk if upstream code changes unexpectedly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is documented in active skill instructions and README examples. The helper implementation is not included in the scanned files, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Bitbucket pipeline failures take time to inspect across logs and builds. This skill helps agents check status, download failed logs, and guide fixes.
actual_capabilities: Check the latest Bitbucket pipeline status through local Node.js helper commands.
Find failed pipeline steps and download failed logs into a local pipeline log folder.
Trigger, stop, and inspect pipelines through bundled Bitbucket CLI wrappers.
Create and manage Bitbucket deployment environments and secured variables when credentials have required scopes.
Help diagnose authentication, scope, and build failures using documented workflows.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Git, npm, and a correctly initialized Bitbucket MCP submodule.
Requires local Bitbucket credentials with scopes that match the requested operation.
Cannot download Bitbucket pipeline artifacts because Bitbucket Cloud does not expose that API.
Runs shell commands and installer scripts, so sensitive environments need manual review first.

use_cases.title: Investigate Failed Builds
use_cases.description: Check the latest failed pipeline, download failed step logs, and summarize likely build causes.

use_cases.title: Operate Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Trigger or stop Bitbucket pipelines and follow their status during deployment work.

use_cases.title: Manage Deployment Settings
use_cases.description: List environments and manage secured deployment variables when scoped credentials are available.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pipeline Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Bitbucket DevOps skill to check the latest pipeline for workspace WORKSPACE and repository REPO. Summarize status, branch, and build number.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Failed Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest failed pipeline for WORKSPACE/REPO, download failed logs, and summarize the likely root cause without printing large logs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deployment Variables
prompt_templates.prompt: List deployment environments for WORKSPACE/REPO, then list secured variables for ENVIRONMENT. Do not reveal secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Run CI Repair Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the failing pipeline, identify the smallest code or configuration fix, ask before editing files, then trigger a new pipeline after approval.

output_examples.input: Check the latest failed pipeline for acme/webapp.
output_examples.output: Pipeline 123 on main failed in the Deploy step. The failed log was saved locally, and the likely issue is a missing deployment variable.

output_examples.input: What failed in build 456 for acme/api?
output_examples.output: Build 456 failed during integration tests. The error summary points to a database connection timeout after the migration step.

output_examples.input: List deployment environments and variables for acme/webapp.
output_examples.output: The repository has Test, Staging, and Production environments. Secured variable names were listed, but secret values were not displayed.

best_practices: Confirm workspace and repository before running any Bitbucket command.
Use the credential check helper instead of opening credential files directly.
Review shell commands before running write, update, or deployment operations.
anti_patterns: Do not paste Bitbucket app passwords or scoped tokens into prompts.
Do not run self-update or installer commands without reviewing the source first.
Do not display full pipeline logs when a short error summary is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Bitbucket account?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs Bitbucket credentials with scopes that match the commands you want to run.

faq.question: Can it download pipeline artifacts?
faq.answer: No. Bitbucket Cloud does not provide an API for downloading pipeline artifacts.

faq.question: Where are pipeline logs stored?
faq.answer: Downloaded logs are stored in a local pipeline log folder inside the current working directory.

faq.question: Does it expose secret variable values?
faq.answer: Secured Bitbucket variable values are write-only through the API and should not be displayed by the skill.

faq.question: Can it manage deployment variables?
faq.answer: Yes, when the credential file uses a token with the required Bitbucket pipeline scopes.

faq.question: Is it safe to install automatically?
faq.answer: No. It uses shell scripts, local credentials, network access, and update commands that need manual review.
